digest.component_or_area: description/body field syncing — rich-text cutover + echo-safety
propositions: After the Cloud cutover, converted ADF descriptions post once and a second reconcile pass emits zero description updates (convergence achieved via codec-idempotent normalize_outbound round-trip).

After the DC cutover, issue.update(fields=…) ships rendered wiki (not raw Markdown) and a second pass emits zero updates; the cutover is gated by a single flag that defaults OFF, restoring plain/identity when disabled.

The emit compare (local-vs-remote) keeps the plain inbound-decoded remote so a pre-cutover legacy body upgrades exactly once; the baseline directionality/conflict compares normalize the LOCAL side through the codec so both operands sit in the decoded space and lossy artifacts cancel.

When both sides edit the body concurrently, the pass keeps rebar's body (local-wins, settled policy) and appends the divergence to the existing conflict_sink, raising an outbound-field-conflict bridge alert so the remote is recorded, never silently destroyed.

The origin-gating guard (outbound only when local != baseline) ensures Jira-authored native constructs survive an unedited body across passes; an inline change-gated 8-byte rich_sha prevents per-pass rewrites on no-op, avoiding the per-pass timestamp churn that plagued epic 0303.
With the marklas extra absent, the cutover emits the plain-text ADF wire (today's behaviour) and raises nothing, degrading gracefully to the existing identity path.
